reviews.scope: solving individual inequalities in the system and graphing intervals on a number line
reviews.reason: Finding the solution set of a system of linear inequalities requires first solving each individual linear inequality and representing its interval on a number line before taking their intersection.

reviews.scope: solving the formulated inequality system to find feasible ranges and plans
reviews.reason: Determining valid allocation plans or parameter ranges from multiple constraints requires solving the resulting system of linear inequalities to identify the common feasible interval.

reviews.scope: translating verbal constraint phrases into inequalities and selecting realistic integer solutions
reviews.reason: Formulating a system of inequalities and choosing realistic integer plans builds directly on translating phrases like at least or at most into individual linear inequalities and applying integer constraints.

reviews.scope: comparing carbon emissions of travel or energy schemes under constraints
reviews.reason: Multi-constraint inequality modeling prepares students to evaluate complex low-carbon plans, but the project criteria only require comparing schemes with inequalities rather than mandatory systems of inequalities.
reviews.counterexample: A student can compare the carbon emissions of two travel or energy schemes using a single linear inequality without setting up a system of inequalities.

reviews.scope: modeling quantitative emission relationships and comparing practical schemes
reviews.reason: Prior experience modeling scheme and allocation word problems with systems of equations helps students structure emission rates and quantitative comparisons in low-carbon living investigations.
reviews.counterexample: Students can model and compare two low-carbon schemes directly with a single-variable equation or linear inequality without using a system of equations.

reviews.scope: distinguishing census and sample survey methods and choosing appropriate survey designs
reviews.reason: Understanding full versus sample surveys and selecting a data collection method according to population characteristics is a survey-design concept unrelated to cross-tabulating data in a two-way table.
reviews.counterexample: Students can distinguish censuses from sample surveys and select an appropriate survey mode from problem contexts without constructing or reading two-way tables.

reviews.scope: identifying the population, individuals, sample, and sample size in a survey
reviews.reason: The concepts of population and sample are defined by contrasting the entire set of investigation objects with the subset drawn during a sample survey.

reviews.scope: evaluating sample representativeness and designing simple random sampling
reviews.reason: Judging whether a sample represents the population fairly and ensuring every individual has an equal selection chance requires identifying the population, individuals, sample, and sample size.

reviews.scope: selecting line charts for change trends and reading line chart data
reviews.reason: Choosing line charts to display temporal trends and extracting analytical information from them directly requires reading values and recognizing increases or decreases on line graphs.

reviews.scope: selecting pie charts for proportions and interpreting sector percentage data
reviews.reason: Choosing pie charts to represent part-to-whole proportions and analyzing their data requires understanding how sector percentages represent shares of a total and computing part quantities.

reviews.scope: organizing raw data into structured summary tables with totals
reviews.reason: Working with two-way tables provides helpful prior familiarity with tabular organization and total checks, but grouping continuous numerical data into a one-way frequency table does not require cross-tabulation.
reviews.counterexample: A one-variable frequency distribution table only groups numerical values into intervals and counts frequencies in a single dimension without two-way classification.

reviews.scope: determining class width and number of classes and completing frequency tables
reviews.reason: Choosing and reading pie, bar, and line charts is a graphical display skill that is unnecessary for grouping raw numerical data into class intervals and tallying a frequency table.
reviews.counterexample: Students can determine range, class width, and class intervals and tally frequencies directly from raw numerical data without using pie, bar, or line charts.

reviews.scope: constructing frequency distribution histograms and reading class frequencies
reviews.reason: Drawing and interpreting a frequency distribution histogram requires organizing continuous data into equal-width class intervals and obtaining the frequency of each class from a frequency distribution table.

reviews.scope: drawing histograms with horizontal class intervals and vertical frequency scales
reviews.reason: Histograms extend bar charts with contiguous numerical intervals on a horizontal axis and frequency bars on a vertical axis, rather than plotting ordered pairs in a four-quadrant Cartesian plane.
reviews.counterexample: Students can construct and read histograms using scaled horizontal and vertical chart axes as in bar charts without Cartesian point coordinates.

reviews.scope: reading time-series data and describing temporal change trends
reviews.reason: Observing how data vary over time and making trend predictions on a trend chart directly builds on reading plotted time-series values and analyzing change trends from line charts.

reviews.scope: describing and explaining temporal patterns in daylight duration with charts
reviews.reason: Investigating how daylight duration changes across dates and describing its seasonal rise-and-fall pattern with charts directly requires reading and interpreting temporal trend charts.

reviews.scope: summarizing the distribution of daylight duration data across the year
reviews.reason: Frequency distribution histograms offer a helpful optional chart representation for comparing how many days fall into different daylight-length intervals across locations during the investigation.
reviews.counterexample: Students can describe and explain how daylight duration varies across dates using a time-series line or trend chart without grouping data into a histogram.

reviews.scope: structuring the daylight duration investigation from data collection to conclusions
reviews.reason: Understanding the general stages of a statistical investigation provides a helpful workflow for planning data collection, organization, charting, and interpretation in the daylight duration project.
reviews.counterexample: Students can collect daylight duration records and plot charts to explain seasonal patterns without formally reciting all six stages of a statistical investigation.

reviews.scope: classifying triangles by angles and recognizing isosceles and equilateral triangles
reviews.reason: Mastering the full classification of triangles by angles into acute, right, and obtuse and by sides into scalene, isosceles, and equilateral directly incorporates primary-level angle and side classification.

reviews.scope: defining a triangle and identifying and denoting its three sides
reviews.reason: A triangle is formed by three line segments connecting non-collinear points, so identifying and symbolizing its sides requires understanding the definition and notation of line segments.

reviews.scope: analyzing side lengths of triangles and checking whether segments form a triangle
reviews.reason: Determining whether three segments can form a triangle and finding side-length ranges, including in isosceles triangles, requires understanding the concept, sides, and classification of triangles.

reviews.scope: justifying that the sum of any two sides exceeds the third side
reviews.reason: Deriving and explaining the triangle inequality theorem directly relies on the fundamental geometric postulate that the line segment between two points is the shortest path.

reviews.scope: expressing and solving for the range of the third side
reviews.reason: Familiarity with inequality notation and solving linear inequalities helps students express third-side bounds and solve problems where triangle side lengths are given as algebraic expressions.
reviews.counterexample: For numerical side lengths, students can find the upper and lower bounds of the third side using simple addition and subtraction without solving linear inequalities.

reviews.scope: identifying vertices and opposite sides and drawing altitudes by triangle type
reviews.reason: Drawing the altitudes of acute, right, and obtuse triangles from each vertex to its opposite side requires knowing triangle elements and distinguishing acute, right, and obtuse triangles.

reviews.scope: defining an altitude and drawing the perpendicular segment from a vertex
reviews.reason: An altitude of a triangle is the perpendicular segment from a vertex to the line containing the opposite side, requiring both the definition and construction of perpendicular lines.

reviews.scope: connecting a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of its opposite side
reviews.reason: Defining and drawing the medians of a triangle requires identifying the vertices and opposite sides of a triangle.

reviews.scope: locating the midpoint of the opposite side and using equal segment lengths
reviews.reason: Constructing a triangle median and understanding why it bisects the opposite side and triangle area directly requires the concept and equal-part property of a segment midpoint.

reviews.scope: identifying interior angles, vertices, and opposite sides of a triangle
reviews.reason: Defining and drawing an angle bisector of a triangle as a segment from a vertex to the opposite side requires knowing the basic elements of a triangle.

reviews.scope: bisecting an interior angle of a triangle and computing related angles
reviews.reason: A triangle angle bisector divides an interior angle into two equal halves, directly requiring the concept, construction, and angle-halving property of an angle bisector.

reviews.scope: identifying the three interior angles of a triangle and finding unknown angles
reviews.reason: Stating the triangle angle sum theorem and solving for unknown angles in various types of triangles requires understanding a triangle and its three interior angles.

reviews.scope: explaining the deductive proof of the triangle angle sum theorem
reviews.reason: Explaining the proof that the three interior angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees requires constructing an auxiliary parallel line and applying parallel line angle properties.

reviews.scope: deriving complementary acute angles in right triangles and its converse
reviews.reason: Both deducing that the two acute angles of a right triangle sum to 90 degrees and proving that a triangle with two complementary angles is right require the 180-degree angle sum theorem.

reviews.scope: deriving exterior angle properties and calculating unknown triangle angles
reviews.reason: Establishing that an exterior angle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles and solving combined interior-exterior angle problems directly depends on the triangle angle sum theorem.

reviews.scope: formulating given and to-prove statements and citing valid deductive reasons
reviews.reason: Translating a geometric proposition into formal Given and To Prove statements and justifying each proof step requires understanding propositions, hypotheses, conclusions, definitions, axioms, and theorems.

reviews.scope: illustrating the standard given, to-prove, and proof format with a concrete theorem
reviews.reason: The proof of the triangle angle sum theorem serves as a familiar exemplar for demonstrating auxiliary lines and step-by-step deductive formatting in geometric proofs.
reviews.counterexample: The standard format of geometric proofs can be taught and practiced using parallel-line or vertical-angle propositions without the triangle angle sum theorem.

reviews.scope: explaining that a triangular plate's center of gravity is the intersection of medians
reviews.reason: Locating the center of gravity of a uniform triangular plate geometrically and explaining why it lies at the intersection of the three medians directly requires mastering triangle medians.

reviews.scope: understanding shape-preserving rigid motion before defining congruent figures
reviews.reason: Knowing that translation preserves size and shape provides intuitive preparation for congruence, but defining congruent figures by superposition and identifying corresponding triangle elements does not require grid translation.
reviews.counterexample: Students can verify figure congruence and match corresponding vertices, sides, and angles through direct superposition, rotation, or reflection without grid translation.

reviews.scope: identifying corresponding vertices, sides, and angles of congruent triangles
reviews.reason: Recognizing congruent triangles, matching their corresponding vertices, sides, and angles, and writing congruence notation requires knowing the fundamental elements of a triangle.

reviews.scope: connecting shape-and-size invariance and corresponding elements under translation to congruence
reviews.reason: Translation properties provide a helpful concrete example of figures that preserve shape and size and introduce corresponding points and segments prior to studying congruent triangles.
reviews.counterexample: Congruent triangles and their corresponding elements can be defined and identified directly through superposition without using translation properties.

reviews.scope: identifying corresponding sides and angles from a triangle congruence statement
reviews.reason: Applying the property that corresponding sides and angles of congruent triangles are equal requires understanding congruence notation and accurately matching corresponding vertices, sides, and angles.

reviews.scope: motivating three-side sufficiency as the converse of six-part congruence properties
reviews.reason: Knowing that congruent triangles have six pairs of equal corresponding parts motivates searching for minimal sufficient conditions, but proving congruence via SSS does not require applying congruence properties.
reviews.counterexample: Proving two triangles congruent by SSS proceeds directly from three given pairs of equal sides to the congruence statement without deducing equal parts from known congruence.

reviews.scope: understanding when three given side lengths determine a valid triangle
reviews.reason: The triangle inequality explains when three given segments can form a triangle during the geometric construction that motivates the SSS congruence criterion.
reviews.counterexample: When applying SSS to prove two existing triangles congruent from equal side lengths, students do not need to check the triangle inequality.

reviews.scope: motivating two-sides-and-included-angle sufficiency as the converse of congruence properties
reviews.reason: Understanding congruence properties helps motivate sufficient conditions for triangle congruence, but identifying an included angle and proving congruence directly via SAS does not require applying congruence properties.
reviews.counterexample: Proving two triangles congruent by SAS uses two pairs of equal sides and their included angles directly without deducing equal parts from a prior congruence.

reviews.scope: following the triangle-construction and superposition inquiry pattern for congruence criteria
reviews.reason: Prior experience exploring SSS through triangle construction and writing a three-condition congruence proof prepares students for investigating and applying the SAS criterion.
reviews.counterexample: SAS is an independent congruence postulate that can be stated, understood, and applied to prove triangles congruent without using SSS.

reviews.scope: motivating angle-and-side congruence conditions as the converse of congruence properties
reviews.reason: Congruence properties provide the converse conceptual background for sufficient congruence criteria, but stating ASA or AAS and proving two triangles congruent directly does not require applying congruence properties.
reviews.counterexample: Proving two triangles congruent by ASA or AAS proceeds directly from two equal angle pairs and a corresponding side pair without deducing parts from known congruence.

reviews.scope: deducing the AAS congruence criterion from ASA using the interior angle sum
reviews.reason: Proving that two triangles with two pairs of equal angles and a pair of equal non-included sides are congruent requires using the triangle angle sum theorem to reduce AAS to ASA.

reviews.scope: motivating right-triangle congruence conditions as the converse of congruence properties
reviews.reason: Knowing the properties of congruent triangles provides converse motivation for congruence criteria, but stating HL and judging when it applies to right triangles does not require applying congruence properties.
reviews.counterexample: Proving two right triangles congruent by HL uses the given right angles, hypotenuses, and legs directly without deducing equal elements from known congruence.

reviews.scope: recognizing right triangles from complementary angles before applying congruence criteria
reviews.reason: Complementary acute angles help identify right triangles when right angles are not explicitly given, but stating HL and applying it when right angles are given does not require acute-angle complementarity.
reviews.counterexample: When two triangles are directly given as right triangles with equal hypotenuses and one pair of equal legs, HL applies without using complementary acute angles.

reviews.scope: contrasting HL with general triangle congruence criteria and understanding side determination
reviews.reason: Familiarity with SSS and earlier congruence criteria helps students recognize when standard three-element criteria do not directly apply and why right triangles admit the HL criterion.
reviews.counterexample: Students can state and apply the HL criterion to two right triangles directly from the hypotenuse and leg conditions without invoking SSS.

reviews.scope: selecting and applying SSS in comprehensive congruence proofs
reviews.reason: Selecting the appropriate congruence criterion from given conditions and supplying missing side conditions in comprehensive proofs requires mastery of the SSS criterion.

reviews.scope: selecting and applying SAS in comprehensive congruence proofs
reviews.reason: Evaluating given side and angle conditions to choose a valid congruence method and write complete proofs requires mastery of the SAS criterion and included angles.

reviews.scope: selecting and applying ASA and AAS in comprehensive congruence proofs
reviews.reason: Choosing among all congruence criteria and completing formal proofs when two pairs of angles and one pair of sides are involved requires mastery of both ASA and AAS.

reviews.scope: selecting and applying HL in comprehensive right-triangle congruence proofs
reviews.reason: Selecting the proper congruence criterion across general and right-triangle problems requires knowing when and how to apply the HL criterion.

reviews.scope: writing complete, properly formatted deductive congruence proofs with reasons
reviews.reason: Writing complete and standardized triangle congruence proofs with explicit justifications for every step directly requires mastering the basic format and deductive norms of geometric proofs.
